title: Risk-reduction of bacteria-transmission into the bloodstream during non-surgical periodontal therapy
summary:
Periodontitis is an inflammatory disease of the periodontium. Among other things, it is maintained by bacteria in plaque below the gums at the roots of the teeth. In addition to the local effects of periodontitis (receding gums, loosening of teeth, loss of teeth, etc.), there is evidence that this disease can have significant effects on overall health. In addition to influences on diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, there is recent evidence of a link between periodontitis, particularly the bacterium Porphyromonas gingivalis, which is one of the lead germs of periodontitis, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease.
The goal of periodontal therapy is to remove the plaque on the roots of the teeth as effectively as possible, which is usually done with hand and/or ultrasonic instruments. However, this inevitably results in bacteria being washed out into the bloodstream. The present research project aims to investigate the bactericidal effect of the blue diode laser with the wavelength of 445 nm before periodontal therapy. One of the objectives of this study is to reduce the bacteria in the adherent plaque and to reduce washout of these bacteria into the bloodstream. In addition, we expect a greater reduction in inflammation of the periodontium by biostimulation using laser treatment. In order to obtain the best possible overview of the potential beneficial effects of the above therapy, this study is planned as a multicenter clinical trial in a half-site comparison. These findings could improve periodontal therapy and thus help later generations of patients.

interventions.name: Before conventional pocket cleaning, the periodontal pockets in the experimental study group are disinfected with a diode laser (wavelength: 445 nm, power: 0.5 W, cw-mode). A 320 µm fiber is used to disinfect circularly around the diseased tooth for 1 minute.
Periodontally diseased teeth are treated with hand instruments and a piezoelectric scaler (conventional pocket cleaning) without prior diode laser disinfection.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimum age 18 years, No periodontal treatment in the last two years, Generalized periodontitis up to stage 3 and grade B, Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who have already received periodontal treatment within the last two years, Pregnancy, Tobacco use, Dental implants, Metabolic disease with possible influence on the healing process, especially diabetes, Patients with infectious diseases, such as HIV, Hep B or Hep C, Patients undergoing chemotherapy, Patients with cystic fibrosis, Antibiosis in the last 3 months
